text.tspan: AWS Transit Gateway: one regional hub instead of a mesh of peerings
One packet from VPC A to VPC B checks THREE route tables:
3 · VPC B subnet route table (for the reply)
Association: each attachment uses exactly ONE TGW route table for traffic coming from it. Propagation: an attachment can add its CIDRs to route tables automatically.
Several route tables = segmentation (e.g. prod can't reach dev). A route table can't hold two routes for the same prefix,
so two VPCs with the same CIDR can't both be reached: that's why overlapping CIDRs need NAT or unique ranges (A2).
